name: SysAdminSuite Protected-Network Endpoint Probe & Identity Gate
sprintRole: Establish fresh protected-network reachability and endpoint identity evidence before any SysAdminSuite mutation, separating network, DNS, directory, and host-state failures instead of guessing from stale inventory
useWhen: A technician or agent must determine whether one or many managed Windows endpoints are actually reachable and correctly identified before deployment, repair, printer, directory, or configuration work, especially when stale directory records, DNS failures, or the wrong network posture can create false conclusions.
inspectFirst: Current SysAdminSuite governance and canonical probe/preflight entrypoint; approved network posture from repository or operator-authorized context; target inventory/hostnames; current DNS resolution; directory/asset identity sources that are explicitly approved; prior fresh receipts; and any current network or endpoint exception policy. Never copy private credentials, secrets, or environment-specific protected-network values into a public prompt artifact.
expectedOutput: A read-only per-target evidence ledger with canonical target identity, DNS result, reachability classification, approved identity/serial confirmation when accessible, freshness timestamp, evidence source, failure class, and the next safe owning workflow. Unresolved, stale-directory, and unreachable targets remain distinct and are not counted as confirmed devices.
nextStep: For each target that passes the network-and-identity gate, route to the exact canonical mutation owner for the requested operation; for every failed or unknown target, preserve the evidence and execute only the bounded diagnostic that can resolve its failure class without mutating the endpoint.
proofGate: No endpoint is declared reachable, present, absent, stale, or correctly identified from memory alone. Each PASS has fresh network plus identity evidence at the supported level; UNKNOWN remains UNKNOWN; DNS, directory, network, privilege, and host failures are not conflated; and the probe performs no target mutation.
copyContent:
PROBE MANAGED WINDOWS ENDPOINTS THROUGH SYSADMINSUITE BEFORE MUTATION. DO NOT GUESS FROM STALE INVENTORY, DIRECTORY PRESENCE, OR A SINGLE PING RESULT.

Repo/product: SysAdminSuite or resolve the active SAS repository from context.
Targets: xyz_hostnames_inventory_or_resolve_from_current_work
Requested downstream action: xyz_deploy_repair_printer_directory_config_or_other
Approved network posture: resolve only from current repository/operator evidence; do not embed private network details into reusable public prompt text.

MISSION
Produce a fresh, read-only endpoint reachability and identity gate that tells the next workflow whether a target is safe to act on. This prompt owns recon and classification, not deployment or repair.

1. RESOLVE THE CANONICAL PROBE OWNER
Read the current SAS governance, command surface, preflight/probe implementation, target resolver, evidence paths, and network policy. Use the repository-owned command rather than inventing an ad hoc ping/nslookup script when a canonical probe exists.

2. ESTABLISH NETWORK POSTURE
Confirm the execution host is on an approved path for the target environment using evidence the repository recognizes. If the current network is wrong, classify the result as a network-posture blocker; do not label the endpoint offline and do not mutate DNS, firewall, trust, VPN, routing, or directory state merely to make the probe pass.

3. RESOLVE EACH TARGET
For every requested hostname or inventory record, capture the canonical target identifier, DNS resolution, and the strongest supported read-only reachability checks. Keep these states separate: RESOLVED_AND_REACHABLE, DNS_UNRESOLVED, RESOLVED_UNREACHABLE, STALE_OR_AMBIGUOUS_DIRECTORY_RECORD, IDENTITY_UNCONFIRMED, PERMISSION_BLOCKED, and UNKNOWN. Use repository-native names when they already exist.

4. CONFIRM IDENTITY
When the workflow requires a serial, asset, computer-account, or other identity check, obtain it only from an approved source. Directory existence alone is not fresh device proof. Do not count a target as confirmed when current network or identity evidence is missing.

5. PRESERVE EVIDENCE
Write or reuse the canonical SAS receipt/report path. Record target, timestamp, execution context, resolver result, evidence source, classification, and next owner. Avoid secrets and sensitive excerpts. For batches, emit a rollup without losing per-host evidence.

6. ROUTE, DO NOT MUTATE
A passed endpoint goes to the exact requested downstream owner. A failed endpoint receives only the smallest read-only diagnostic that can resolve its class. Do not install software, change AutoLogon, map printers, move directory objects, reboot, or clean remote state in this prompt.

VALIDATE
Prove the probe is read-only, uses the canonical SAS target/network resolver, preserves UNKNOWN honestly, distinguishes DNS/network/directory/identity failures, and produces fresh per-target evidence.

DELIVER
Report the per-target classification ledger, evidence location, confirmed targets, unresolved/blocked targets, proof ceiling, and the exact next owning workflow for each class.
